classification.difficultyReason: Substantial transfer, coordinated cases or justification beyond a direct worked-example substitution. Only the first coordinate is bounded; closed endpoints include both vertical edges.

content.prompt:
Let $A$ and $B$ be two sets. The $\mathit{Cartesian\ product}$ of $A$ and $B$ is the set of all ordered pairs from $A$ and $B$.
$$A\times B=\{(a,b)\text{ where }a\in A,\ b\in B\}.$$
List the elements of, or describe geometrically, $A\times B$ for the following sets.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=[-1,1]\\B&=\mathbb R\end{aligned}$$

answer.short:
The infinite vertical strip $-1\le x\le1$, including the boundary lines $x=-1$ and $x=1$.

Only the first coordinate is bounded.
answer.worked:
The first coordinate satisfies $-1\le x\le1$, while the second may be any real number:
$$A\times B=\{(x,y)\text{ where }-1\le x\le1,\ y\in\mathbb R\}.$$
This is the infinite vertical strip between $x=-1$ and $x=1$, including both boundary lines.
